function.name: calculate_time
function.description: Calculates the time taken to cover a distance at a certain speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance.description: The distance to be covered in meters. This is a float type value.

speed.description: The speed at which the object is moving in m/s. This is a float type value.

round_to_nearest_second.description: Optional parameter to round the time to the nearest second.

message.content: I’m sorry—I don’t have direct access to your device’s clock or an external time service, so I can’t tell you the precise current time. If you let me know what time zone you’re interested in (or whether you’d like UTC), I can explain how to find it on most devices or give you a general idea of where you stand relative to standard times.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What's the time right now?" We need current time. But we don't have real-time capability; but maybe we can approximate using system clock or mention it's not possible. According to policy, we should respond with best effort and say cannot provide exact due to no access. Provide local time if known? Probably can't. So answer politely.

We might also ask clarifying question about timezone. We'll comply.
